newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended lower on Monday, as the weak tone of other European and the U.S. market continued to sap the market of vitality.

"We have moved practically in step with the central markets," said Alfredo Urrutia, economist at Societe Generale in Madrid. "The U.S. markets are continuing to take profits and they are still digesting the indicators from Friday."

The domestic market, largely content with Spanish economic performance, disregarded domestic news that Spanish producer prices fell 0.1 percent in June and that unemployment would fall by more than 80,000 people in July.
The market is looking ahead to auctions on Tuesday of three-year and 10-year debt for a maximum of 350 billion and 450 billion pesetas, respectively.
On Wednesday, five and 15-year debt and one-year and 18-month bills will be auctioned.
